title: Cover All Nodes With the Fewest Separate Paths

concept.title: Each edge that joins two path pieces saves one path: the answer is n minus a maximum matching
body: A directed acyclic graph is given. Cover **all nodes** with paths so that every node lies on **exactly one** path (the paths do not share nodes, and a path of a single node is allowed). What is the smallest number of paths? With no edge used we need `n` paths (one per node). Every edge `u -> v` that we use to **join** the end of one path to the start of another saves one path. Each node can be followed by at most one used edge (its out-edge) and preceded by at most one (its in-edge).

This is a matching problem. Build a bipartite graph with **two copies of every node**: a left copy `u_out` and a right copy `v_in`, and an edge `u_out - v_in` for each edge `u -> v` of the DAG. A set of used edges in which no node has two out-edges and no node has two in-edges is exactly a **matching** in this bipartite graph. (No cycle can appear, because the graph is acyclic, so the used edges always form paths.) So the largest number of joins is the size of a maximum matching, and

body.code: minimum number of paths = n - (size of a maximum matching)

body: The maximum matching is found by augmenting paths, as in the previous task. With `n <= 500` and `m <= 3000` it takes about `n * m` = 1.5 million steps. For example, a single long path of `n` nodes has a matching of size `n - 1`, hence one path; `n` nodes without edges have an empty matching, hence `n` paths.

statement: A directed acyclic graph has `n` nodes and `m` edges. A path cover is a set of paths (a path may consist of a single node) such that every node belongs to exactly one path. Print the smallest possible number of paths in a path cover.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the number of nodes (numbered 1 to n) and the number of edges.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge that goes from the node `u` to the node `v`.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of paths.
constraints: The graph has no directed cycle.
There are no self-loops and no repeated edges.

examples.note: The paths 1, 2 and 3, 4 cover all four nodes with 2 paths; one path is not enough because node 1 has two successors: 2.

hints: Split every node into a left copy (outgoing) and a right copy (incoming).
Each edge u -> v becomes an edge from the left copy of u to the right copy of v.
The answer is n minus the size of a maximum matching of this bipartite graph.

solution.complexity: Time O(n * m), space O(n + m).
